title: How to reset a tripped GFCI outlet
summary: Unplug the load, press RESET on the outlet with the TEST/RESET buttons, then plug back in. If it will not stay reset, stop and find the fault.

blocks.title: Unplug, press RESET, plug back in
blocks.body: A tripped GFCI has popped its internal breaker. Clearing the load and pressing RESET is the whole job when the outlet is healthy.

blocks.heading: Reset sequence
items: Unplug whatever was in the outlet (and anything on downstream outlets it protects).
Press RESET firmly until it clicks and stays in. The outlet should now have power.
Plug the device back in. If RESET will not stay down, or trips again immediately, leave it unplugged and troubleshoot the device or the circuit — do not keep forcing it.

blocks.title: If it will not reset
blocks.body: A GFCI that refuses to reset, or trips with nothing plugged in, is telling you about a ground fault or a failed device. Kill the breaker, stop using the circuit, and get a qualified person if you are not sure.
